design_rationale:
WORKLOG task 0 (residential_gas_care), kept from Step 0 onward.

[Step 0 draw] draw_counts.py --task 0 printed {"prerequisite_problems": 1, "problems": 2, "factor_counts": [5, 5]}. Tree = root gas_ext_added_premise_rate (5 factors) <- gas_ext_recontract_rate (5 factors). Difficulty-wide draw (--tasks 2): task 1 = 3 prerequisite problems, factor counts [6,4,4,5].

[Scope snapshot] Occupied before this task: nothing. Claimed here: gas_ext_recontract_rate (gas_renew, owner=user tool accept_gas_recontract_offer_a9611340) and gas_ext_added_premise_rate (gas_enroll, agent tool enroll_gas_added_premise_5ded636b). Left for task 1: the in-term renewal acceptance (a different gas_renew situation: election on or before the contract end date), the sign-up credit, the renewal loyalty credit and the latest-bill rebill credit (gas_credit / gas_adjustment), which need an agreement still in its term. Constraint discovered at Step 0 and recorded: the only customer-owned gas events are rescission, cancellation, its withdrawal and renewal acceptance (blueprint summary), and only the renewal carries a number, so both tasks' customer writes are renewal elections, split by the base gas_renewal rule's own two situations (on/before contract end vs after rollover within the grace period). A rolled-over agreement no longer carries the plan it was on (variant becomes Monthly Variable), so a credit or correction on it cannot be priced from records; the re-contract therefore can only be a prerequisite of something priced from the re-contracted agreement, which is the added-premise enrollment.

[Why a good test] Surface goal: 'gas service at the cottage'. Hidden: (1) the household rate is fixed only after the home agreement, once rolled over, again carries a term - the agent must see in find_gas_agreements that the home agreement rolled over on 2026-03-11 (term 0, no end date) and work out from the re-contract rule that the customer's own re-contract within the grace period is the one write that brings that state about; (2) the re-contract rate needs notice-compliance arithmetic (54 vs 21 days), the held-rate average, the grace day count, the offered plan, the peak cycle and the electricity relationship; (3) the household rate is then computed on the re-contracted agreement (0.7340, Price Lock 24, end 2028-03-25), reading 12-month gas usage, tenure, 12-month electricity energy charges, remaining term and the new plan change date. Depth 2 problems, breadth 10 factors over gas notices, gas ledger, power holding and power ledger.

[Problem-tree card] edge gas_ext_added_premise_rate -> gas_ext_recontract_rate: kind value_input, gate binding home_rate, form state, sentence 'The household rate for an added premise is fixed only after the home agreement, once rolled over, again carries a term in months and a contract end date.' Four-point test: ordering connective 'only after'; record-visible state (term in months, contract end date); no tool/id/code token; scope exact (only a rolled-over home agreement). Exactly one write of this difficulty brings that state about on a rolled-over agreement: the re-contract (the in-term renewal applies only on or before the contract end date; there is no plan-change policy in this charter). Opening evidence: gas_agreements.394a0e01-2e87-4700-94b9-a7ef863be771.term_months=0, contract_end_date='', plan_change_date=2026-03-11, variant Monthly Variable. Resolving owner: user. Deletion sensitivity (Step 5 run): without the re-contract the household rate is 0.6850 instead of 0.6890 and the home agreement keeps its opening plan/term/rate. Topological order: re-contract (step 9) then enrollment (step 11). user_scenario never names the rollover, a term, a rate or the re-contract; the acceptance appears only in a branch triggered by the agent's explanation. Tools validate nothing (see prerequisite_closure.tools_do_not_block).

[Base-invariant card] gas_renew: gas_renewal.renewal_active (status active - gas_agreements.394a0e01-2e87-4700-94b9-a7ef863be771.status=active); gas_renewal.gas_post_expiry_grace (anchor gas_agreements.plan_change_date 2026-03-11, +30 calendar days, inclusive, not_after: window closes end of 2026-04-10; election 2026-03-26 = day 15 -> satisfied; 2026-04-11 would fail). gas_enroll: gas_agg_multi_holding.one_live_gas_agreement_per_premise (no gas agreement on premise 08c4a4cb-51aa-44e5-a679-7d3a03c300ee; the only gas agreement is on the home premise), gas_enrollment_eligibility.residential_gas_premise (premise_class residential), cap_customer_gas_plan (assistance_program none), channel phone allowed for Price Lock 24. Overwrites declared: gas_expiry_notices 'when the two notices differ, the final_options_notice governs' replaced by the notice-protection sentence; gas_renewal 'takes the offered plan, its term_months and the offered renewal rate' replaced by the re-contract sentence; gas_enrollment_eligibility offer-rate sentence replaced by the household-rate sentence. All other base clauses inherited (term start on election date, end-date counting rule, no ETF, no sign-up credit).

[Business-object card] Re-contract object: home agreement 394a0e01-2e87-4700-94b9-a7ef863be771 (premise 2217 Northwest Boulevard). Enrollment object: cottage premise 08c4a4cb-51aa-44e5-a679-7d3a03c300ee (4512 Walnut Road, Buckeye Lake); the computation acts on the home agreement. Rows aggregated: home energy lines with billing_period_start after 2025-03-26 (11 lines, 926 therms; the 2025-03-11 line, 118 therms, is the window near-miss), all 24 energy lines for the peak (208 therms, 2026-01-11), power energy lines with billing_period_start after 2025-03-26 (11 lines, 1211.66 USD; the 12 power service-fee lines and the 2025-03-06 cycle, 94.38 USD, are excluded).

[Factor card - re-contract] notice_protection (method; tier 'exactly one notice non-compliant'; evidence notices 26183684-ce05-4e79-b0db-8f499b6b479c 2026-01-15 lead 54 and bc50d412-aa7e-4a7a-b448-bafbc43d5873 2026-02-17 lead 21; baseline final rate -> result 0.7890); prompt_return (parameter; 15 days; 0.0050; baseline -> 0.7390); commitment (parameter; offered Price Lock 24; 0.0100; baseline -> 0.7440); winter_peak (parameter; 208 therms; adder 0.0100; baseline -> 0.7240); electricity_relationship (parameter, cross-difficulty power, multi-source status AND days; 2502 days; 0.0150; baseline -> 0.7490). Whole baseline 0.8090. Gold 0.7340.
[Factor card - household rate] household_form (method; fixed plan AND 926 therms; x0.97 -> 0.7120; baseline -> 0.7110); household_tenure (parameter; 745 days; 0.0080; near-miss: only 15 days over the 730 line; baseline -> 0.6970); household_electricity (parameter, cross-difficulty power ledger; 1211.66; 0.0060; baseline -> 0.6950); term_alignment (parameter; 730 days to 2028-03-25; 0.0050; baseline -> 0.6940); new_commitment (parameter, multi-source days AND term; 0 days, term 24; 0.0040; baseline -> 0.6930). Whole baseline 0.7340. Gold 0.6890.

[Persona design] Diane Hollister, retired librarian, warm and scattered; volunteers only the cottage goal and 'whatever terms go with the house'; phone, SSN last four, ZIP, cottage address and gas account number only when asked; admits not knowing her plan or rate; accepts the renewal offer only after the agent explains the house account must be handled; runs the handed-over action with the agent's values; stops when told the cottage enrollment is submitted.

[Standard solution] find_customers(phone) -> verify(phone, 2593) -> find_premises -> find_gas_agreements (rollover found) -> find_gas_notices -> find_gas_billing -> find_power_agreements -> find_power_billing -> unlock/hand over re-contract (Price Lock 24, 24, 0.7340, 2028-03-25) -> unlock/call enrollment (cottage, Price Lock 24, 24, 0.6890).

[Verification run] /tmp authoring helper replaying gold with the real tools and check_compute's evaluator printed: recontract result 0.734 baseline 0.809 sens notice_protection 0.789, prompt_return 0.739, commitment 0.744, winter_peak 0.724, electricity_relationship 0.749; household result 0.689 baseline 0.734 sens 0.711/0.697/0.695/0.694/0.693; household without the re-contract 0.685. Gates run for --task 0: EXTENDED OK, TASK TOOL CONTRACT OK, REPLAY OK (12 actions, closure 56 rows), SOLVABILITY OK (5 base gates, 28 seed rows), COMPUTE OK (10 factors, 2 cross), GROUNDING OK, SCOPE OK; check_traceability deferred until the KB is published.

[Easy mistakes] using the final options rate without the notice protection (0.7890 path); counting 12 months of usage including the 2025-03-11 cycle; adding power fee lines; computing the cottage rate on the opening home rate 0.6990 (0.6850) because the re-contract was not done first; taking the household rate before the re-contract end date exists (term alignment 0).

[Draft recomputation from visible context] Using only the rules (as published), the finders' returns and the persona: the agent can see the rollover, read the prerequisite sentence, find in the re-contract rule that a rolled-over customer within the grace period re-contracts on the final options plan, compute 0.7340, hand it over, then compute 0.6890 on the updated record; no second reading found.

[Round 2 revisions] T0-F1 (stamp agreeing with the tier): symptom premises.annual_therm_usage = 926 equalled the rule's 12-month energy-line sum; root cause the premise attribute was seeded from the same ledger; change: the home premise now carries the utility's stale 12-month figure 868 from enrollment, which contradicts the ledger and would put a stamp-reader on the 500–899 household tier (base 0.7240, household rate 0.7010) instead of the ledger's 926 therms (≥ 900); no rule reads the stamp. The near-miss observation is thereby also strengthened: the one record a careless reader reaches for now flips the tier. O-1: all rate and credit computes now round exactly half up (int(x*10^n+0.5)), matching the rules; this world has no tie, so every scored and sensitivity figure is unchanged (0.7340, 0.6890 and the ten factor figures). Gates re-run for task 0 and difficulty-wide: green.
user_scenario:
You are Diane Hollister, a retired middle-school librarian in Columbus, Ohio. You and your husband just closed on a small lake cottage at Buckeye Lake, and you are calling Beacon Ridge Energy because you want Beacon Ridge gas service at the cottage too. You open warmly but a little scattered, saying you already get your gas and electricity at the house from Beacon Ridge and you would like gas service at the cottage set up with them as well, on whatever terms go with the house. You want the agent to take care of the cottage sign-up for you on this call; you are not shopping around and you do not need anything mailed.

You do not volunteer account details in a lump. When the agent asks how to find you, you give your phone number, 6145550126. If they ask you to confirm who you are, you give the last four of your Social Security number, 2593, and, only if they ask for something more, your ZIP code, 43221. If they want the cottage address you say it is 4512 Walnut Road, Buckeye Lake, Ohio 43008, and that Columbia Gas of Ohio already serves it; if they ask for the gas account number there, you read it off the closing paperwork as 1712093-2655. If asked about your house, it is 2217 Northwest Boulevard in Columbus. You have no idea what plan the house is on or what it costs per therm; you pay the bill and file the letters, and you say exactly that if asked.

Only if the agent explains that something has to be taken care of on the house account before the cottage can be priced, you listen, say the letters from earlier in the year probably went into the pile on your desk, and when they lay out that you can still take the offer you agree that you will accept the renewal offer from the letter for the house, because you want the house locked in again anyway. When the agent hands the house action over to you to complete yourself, you do it exactly as they give it to you, with the plan, term, rate and end date they read out, and you tell them it went through and read back what you see. You never suggest figures yourself.

If the agent quotes you a rate for the cottage, you say that sounds fine and ask them to go ahead and put the cottage in. If a figure they mention sounds different from something they said earlier, you just ask them to double-check it against the account; you never offer a number of your own. Once the agent tells you the cottage enrollment has been submitted, you thank them, say you will watch for the utility's letter, and end the call.

edges.condition: The home gas agreement, whose plan change date records a rollover to month-to-month service, carries a term in months above zero and a non-empty contract end date written by a re-contract within the post-expiry grace period.
edges.policy_source: The household rate for an added premise is fixed only after the home agreement, once rolled over, again carries a term in months and a contract end date.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: The home agreement rolled over to Beacon Ridge Gas Monthly Variable on 2026-03-11 and carries term 0 and no contract end date at the held rate 0.6990.
unresolved_at_frozen_time.flips_to_true_by: The re-contract at step 9 writes variant Beacon Ridge Gas Price Lock 24, term_months 24, contract_end_date 2028-03-25, contract rate 0.7340 and plan_change_date 2026-03-26; the household rate then reads home_rate 0.7340 instead of 0.6990.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: Single chain: the household rate has one prerequisite, so the only topological order is the re-contract (step 9) then the cottage enrollment (step 11). The enrollment writes a new agreement row and never touches the home agreement, so nothing written later can change the re-contract.

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Skipping the re-contract leaves the home agreement on Monthly Variable at 0.6990 with no end date: the household rate recomputes to 0.6850 instead of 0.6890 (household form falls to the home rate because the plan is not fixed, term alignment and new commitment fall to 0), and the home agreement's variant, term, rate, end date and plan change date stay at their opening values instead of Price Lock 24 / 24 / 0.7340 / 2028-03-25 / 2026-03-26.

prerequisite_closure.no_user_hint: user_scenario asks only for gas service at the cottage on whatever terms go with the house; it never mentions the rollover, the renewal letters' content, a re-contract, a term or a rate. The only mention of accepting the renewal offer sits in a conditional branch that fires after the agent explains something must be done on the house account first.
prerequisite_closure.tools_do_not_block: enroll_gas_added_premise_5ded636b (task_tools.py) creates the enrollment_pending agreement with whatever plan, term and rate it is given and never reads the home agreement; called before the re-contract it would still write a row (at the wrong rate). accept_gas_recontract_offer_a9611340 only updates the named agreement and checks nothing.
